item.research_question: How does high-strain compression versus tensile loading affect atomistic clustering and ordering transitions in Al0.1CrCoFeNi, and what is the role of thermo-plastic instability?
item.material_system: Quinary Al0.1CrCoFeNi high-entropy alloy (Al mole fraction x = 0.10)
item.processing_route: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using a hybrid Embedded Atom Method (EAM) and Lennard-Jones (LJ) potential; initial melt at 2,200 K, quenched at 21.11 K/ps to target temperatures (77–1,000 K), followed by uniaxial deformation at a strain rate of 10^10 s^-1 to 0.9% engineering strain
item.test_conditions: Temperatures: 77 K, 300 K, 700 K, 1,000 K; Loading modes: Dynamic compression and tension; Strain rate: 10^10 s^-1; Strain: up to 0.9%; Simulation cell: 62,500 atoms in FCC lattice (2.5 nm x 2.5 nm x 2.5 nm)
key_findings: Under compressive loading, a peak flow stress of ~125 MPa is recorded at 77 K and 300 K, dropping to ~90 MPa at 700 K and 1,000 K.
High-strain compression induces a clustering-to-ordering transition, evidenced by increased unlike pair correlations (e.g., Al-Co, Al-Cr) and decreased like pair correlations (e.g., Al-Al).
No clustering-to-ordering transition occurs under tensile loading; the clustering phase dominates, inducing plastic flow similar to a wire-drawing process.
Large stress fluctuations at elevated temperatures under compression are attributed to thermo-plastic instability in the shear band.
Strain hardening is observed under compressive loading but is absent under tensile deformation across the temperature range.
The Al-Ni pair exhibits the strongest interchange-energy fluctuations at a long-wavelength (k = [000]), driving Al-Al and Ni-Ni clustering.
The calculated spinodal temperature (T_sp) is 840 K, showing good agreement with the experimentally observed transition temperature of 813–823 K.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the clustering-to-ordering transition under compression to atomistic rearrangements driven by high-strain deformation, which increases unlike pair correlations. The large fluctuations and thermal softening at high temperatures are explained by thermo-plastic instability in the shear band, leading to shear-induced disordering similar to bulk metallic glasses.
item.limitations: The high strain rate of 10^10 s^-1 used in MD simulations is chosen for computational feasibility and restricts the use of experimentally-realizable high strain rates (~10^2 s^-1).
item.future_work: The investigation provides further motivation for the experimental exploration of high-temperature compressive thermo-plastic instability in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
quotes: High-strain compression promotes atomistic rearrangements in Al 0.1 CrCoFeNi, resulting in a clustering-to-ordering transition that is absent for tensile loading.
Large fluctuations under stress, and at higher temperatures, are attributed to the thermo-plastic instability in Al 0.1 CrCoFeNi.
The transition to ordering state among the different elements of the Al 0.1 CrCoFeNi is possible only for the high compressive strain condition.
